messages:
sara: Quick heads-up — I pushed a PRD draft to the repo titled 'Tenant Access Surface: scoped keys + project mapping'. Asking for a quick read: acceptance criteria, edge cases, and launch gating. Main ask: agree which items are must-block for GA.

jon: Thanks — link? I can't find it in the roadmap board.

sara: https://stash/repo/rfd/tenant-access-surface.md — start at the 'Launch gating' section. TL;DR: customers (FinCorp, Acme) require per-project API keys, revocation API, audit logs >= 1y, KMS integration, and model access allowlist.

priya: skimming — one early note: we have many third-party integrators that use long-lived API keys. Migration plan needs to avoid breaking them. Suggest automatic dual-keys + grace period.

mike: Beta rollout suggestion: 1) opt-in beta for 10 tenants, 2) enable scoped keys only for new keys initially, 3) migrate existing keys with 90-day grace and telemetry to catch failures. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

elaine: From an acceptance perspective, propose the following pass/fail checks:
- Revocation endpoint returns 200 and invalidates tokens within 1s for active requests (observed via trace id).
- Audit logs contain: actor, key_id, org_id, project_id, models_requested, timestamp.
- KMS-wrapped secrets and rotation policy exercised in staging.

jon: A few security concerns:
1) DB migration: we need to add project_id on keys table and backfill. Backfill must be reversible.
2) Token format: make scoped keys parseable without an expensive lookup so gateways can enforce model allowlists.
3) Revoke must propagate to caches (edge + runtime) — propose an in-memory revocation TTL + streaming invalidation.

priya: Edge cases:
- Keys embedded in long-lived serverless containers (no easy redeploy). We should provide short-lived scoped tokens + a token-exchange endpoint for servers to exchange long-lived creds for scoped ones.
- Tokens appearing in logs/prompts. We must mask in logs and add a model-probing guard (reject tokens in prompt payloads).

elaine: Example token schema suggestion for fast parse: `rwd:org:{org_id}:proj:{proj_id}:v{ver}:{random}` — gateway extracts org/proj from prefix. Also doc shows sample API: 
```
POST /v1/keys/revoke
{
  "key_id": "rwd:org:123:proj:456:v1:abcd",
  "reason": "compromise"
}
```

jon: For propagation: we'll emit a revocation event to the streaming bus and set an in-memory blacklist entry on runtimes with TTL of 2m to allow fast denial. Full authority is from central store. We'll add a migration job that marks existing keys as `unscoped` and writes a `proj_id = NULL` until owner maps.

deploy-bot: CI: PR #482 added schema migration `add_project_id_to_keys` — migration job must be scheduled during low traffic window.

mike: For launch gating prioritization: my vote for MUST: revocation API, audit logging, and KMS integration. NICE: automatic migration tooling, token-exchange endpoint, per-project rate-limits.

priya: Threat model addition: lateral movement scenario where leaked key allows access to multiple projects in same org. We must ensure scoped keys are minimized in blast radius. Consider defaulting to project-scoped for all new keys.

jon: DB impact estimate: keys table adds one column + index on (org_id, proj_id). Backfill will touch ~3M rows — plan for chunked job with checkpointing. Will create RFC patch for migration strategy.

elaine: QA plan: unit tests for parsing, e2e test for revoke propagation in staging, chaos run where we expire keys mid-request, and synthetic telemetry checks for audit completeness.

sara: Great feedback. Next steps: jon — draft migration RFC and revocation design doc by EOD Wed. priya — write threat-model appendix. elaine — consolidate acceptance criteria into checklist. mike — coord with a couple of PM beta customers for opt-in. We'll meet Thurs 10am to decide MUST vs NICE and finalize GA gating. :calendar:

jon: Ack. I'll drop a link to the RFC here when ready.

priya: Ack — will add examples of worst-case leak scenarios.

mike: I'll ping Acme & FinCorp.

sara: Thanks all — pushing updated PRD after meeting. :thumbsup:
